text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Labour unions are stepping up their protest against a pension system reform planned by the government in a bid reduce the country's budget deficit.
- Sugar producer Agrana says it cannot compete with other producers without using gene-technolgy. However it will not use gene-manipulated plants in Austria.

- The European Commission has accepted Stet's takeover of a 25 percent stake in Post & Telekom Austria's (PTA) mobile phone company mobilkom. PTA has protested against a draft telecommunications law that would force it to offer its services to other telecom providers for free when the market is liberalised.
- Milkproducers Bergland and Obersteirische plan to invest 500 million schillings in a joint warehouse in Styria.
- Michael Haeupl, Vienna's mayor, says Bank Austria must gradually move away from politics. A study on the privatisation of the City of Vienna's stake in Bank Austria should be ready by late autumn.
- Regional energy provider EVN says hopes for lower gas prices will not be fulfilled when the European market is liberalised.

- Members of the conservative People's Party and the far-right Freedom Party have harshly criticised Green politician Peter Pilz for speaking to the U.S. Congress about the escape of the alleged Iranian murderers of three Kurdish opposition leaders in Vienna in 1989.
- Interior Minister Karl Schloegl says Austria will keep Bosnian refugees until June 1998.
- Retail chain Meinl plans to go public at Budapest's stock exchange without increasing its capital. The company plans to expand its activities to Romania.
DIE PRESSE

- Styria's vice-state leader Peter Schachner-Blazizek said in Brussels the European Union's eastward expanion should be realised in the next five to six years. He criticised Austria's lack of interest in the expansion.
- Pensioned civil servants might lose up to 10,000 schillings should the government's plans for the reform of the country's public pension schemes go ahead.
- The European Commission is expected to take legal action against Austria's anonymous savings accounts at the European Court of Justice.
- Retail turnover was only down 0.3 percent in the first quarter of 1997, while the savings rate is declining. Spending is expected to rise slightly this year even though income was down.
KURIER
- After three years Austrians see more disadvantages in the country's membership in the European Union, a study says.
- Vienna's aiport Flughafen Wien spent 375 million schillings in preparation for Austria joining the European Union's Schengen agreement.

- Oil and chemicals producer OMV plans to search for oil and gas in northern Africa. The company has scrapped its plans to bid for Upper Austria's stake in its regional energy provider OKA. U.S. Eurogas will take over OMV's unit in Yakutia.
- Austria will exactly meet the Maastricht criteria on deficit this year, an OECD-report says.
NEUE KRONENZEITUNG
- One day of striking by Austria's civil servants costs 280 million schillings, the newspaper reports.
